title: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips
title_en: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips
author: Katie Tarasov
content_snippet:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.

"Resilient supply on the foundry is very important,"Tan said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer,"Tan added, without naming the debut client.

It's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. After years of missteps

author: Louise Matsakis
content_snippet:
This week, the Trump administration made it significantly harder for Chinese companies to access some of the world’s most advanced AI chips. For years, tech firms like Alibaba and ByteDance could rent computing power from data centers overseas, allowing them to use powerful Nvidia chips they were generally prohibited from physically importing into China. This is known as remote access.

But under new plans announced on Monday, overseas data centers that want to provide large amounts of computing
summary_en: The Trump administration has mandated special licensing for overseas data centers providing large-scale computing power to China, effectively closing the 'remote access' loophole. Additional export controls were imposed on Singapore and Malaysia to curb chip smuggling, a move triggered by the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his ties to Chinese intelligence assets.

title_en: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
author: Teresa Elsey
content_snippet:
Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack .

You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nausea

author: Bloomberg
content_snippet:
The malfunctions have undermined confidence in key systems used for essential tasks.

SAN FRANCISCO – Technology failures disrupting everything from Americans’ air travel and banking transactions to secretive work at the US National Security Agency are fuelling public distrust and paranoia about ageing tech infrastructure – even with no sign the episodes are linked or the work of malicious actors.

Breakdowns over the past week have caused enough havoc to spur American consumers into a panic-buy
summary_en: Recent high-profile system outages across the NSA, FAA, and Microsoft have paralyzed essential services, fueling public anxiety despite no evidence of malicious cyber-attacks. Senator Mark Warner emphasized that AI-driven vulnerability discovery is forcing organizations to push updates at an unsustainable pace, exposing the systemic fragility of aging digital infrastructure.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 近期包括美国国家安全局（NSA）、联邦航空管理局（FAA）及微软公司在内的多方关键系统相继发生技术故障，导致金融、民航及内部通信大面积瘫痪。参议员马克·沃纳指出，AI加速了系统脆弱性探测的频率，导致企业与机构在应对瞬时补丁更新时不堪重负，基础设施的韧性已无法承载当前数字化转型的极端速率。

Senator Mark Warner emphasized that AI-driven vulnerability discovery is forcing organizations to push updates at an unsustainable pace, exposing the systemic fragility of aging digital infrastructure.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】美国国家安全局（NSA）、联邦航空管理局（FAA）、微软公司、弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员马克·沃纳在美国境内关键数字化基础设施：系统性宕机导致服务中断及公众恐慌性消费，引发政界对于AI辅助攻防压力过载的关注
【起因与机理】AI驱动的自动化漏洞扫描与修复周期错位，导致基础设施在不堪重负的状态下崩塌
【核心事实细节】核心事件：跨领域关键信息系统连续多日发生不明原因故障。

fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] NSA, FAA, Microsoft, and Senator Mark Warner (US critical digital infrastructure): Widespread system outages and public panic buying triggered by concerns over infrastructure reliability
[Root Cause & Mechanism] AI-accelerated vulnerability scanning forces unsustainable patch management cycles, straining legacy systems
[Key Metrics] In the wake of the FAA failures, the Trump administration is seeking US$50.

[Industry Impact & Outlook] Outlook: Policymakers are highlighting the structural tension between AI-accelerated vulnerability detection and the inability of legacy systems to handle rapid patch management.

title: F.A.A. Shelves Routers Like the One Linked to the Nationwide Ground Stop

content_snippet: Federal officials said they believed that a router made by Juniper Networks caused a data overload that disrupted communications.
summary_en: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation and operation of Juniper Networks routers, following findings that a recently installed unit in El Dorado, Arkansas, contributed to last week's nationwide air traffic control ground stop. content_snippet: The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.'s ability to find gaping security holes in popular software.

author: Mia Sato
content_snippet:
Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.

Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit a
summary_en: Alexandr Wang, Chief AI Officer at Meta, recently posted an AI-generated video on Instagram featuring fictitious video calls between Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Although the clip is labeled as AI-generated per platform requirements, it has intensified concerns regarding how deepfake technology blurs the line between reality and fabrication, posing risks to public figure integrity.
